newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon debt widens on TI buy, few trades.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon debt widens on TI buy, few trades.

text.p: Raytheon Co's $2.95 billion all-cash bid for Texas Instrument Inc's defense assets fostered cautious sentiment among debt market players Monday, traders and analysts said.
Bids for Raytheon's 10-year outstanding debt widened five basis points at the open to 60 bid, 55 offer, though few transactions were reported by midday.
Raytheon's outstanding debentures of 2025 were not quoted as of midday.

Spreads have dropped by about 15 basis points since October, however, based on the Street's anticipation that such a deal would significantly increase the company's debt load, according to one Wall Street investment bank debt analyst.
The analyst said a successful stock bid by Raytheon for General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp would buffer that highly-leveraged position.
Raytheon and Northrop Grumman Corp are believed to be the only bidders for Hughes.

"The end game is not here yet with a big property (Hughes) still out there," the analyst said. "If Hughes goes for the price-tag of $8 billion to $9 billion, Northrop or Raytheon probably do not want to finance that with debt, so obviously if it's Raytheon their leverage will go down."
Raytheon said its debt would total $6.6 billion after the TI deal, for a debt-to-capital ratio of 59 percent.
One analyst estimated Raytheon's debt-to-capital ratio at 40 percent as of the 1996 fourth quarter.
